cards.quote: The SHGs promote thrift in small proportions by a minimum contribution from each member. From the pooled money, credit is given to the needy members to be repayable in small instalments at reasonable interest rates.

source.section: 5.3 Credit and Marketing in Rural Areas

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: SHGs get a renovating fund to take up self-employment for income generation. What are such credit provisions called?
cards.back: Such credit provisions are generally referred to as micro-credit programmes.
cards.quote: renovating fund to take up self employement for income generation. Such credit provisions are generally referred to as micro-credit programmes.

source.section: 5.3 Credit and Marketing in Rural Areas

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: In recent years, all the adults are encouraged to open bank accounts as a part of a scheme known as ____.
cards.back: In recent years, all the adults are encouraged to open bank accounts as a part of a scheme known as JanDhan Yojana.
cards.quote: In recent years, all the adults are encouraged to open bank accounts as a part of a scheme known as JanDhan Yojana.

source.section: 5.3 Credit and Marketing in Rural Areas

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: What is agricultural marketing?
cards.back: Agricultural marketing is a process that involves the assembling, storage, processing, transportation, packaging, grading and distribution of different agricultural commodities across the country.
cards.quote: Agricultural marketing is a process that involves the assembling, storage, processing, transportation, packaging, grading and distribution of different agricultural commodities across the country.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Name the marketing problems farmers faced prior to independence.
cards.back:
faulty weighing and manipulation of accounts
did not have the required information on prices prevailing in markets were often forced to sell at low prices
did not have proper storage facilities to keep back their produce for selling later at a better price
cards.quote: suffered from faulty weighing and manipulation of accounts. Farmers who did not have the required information on prices prevailing in markets were often forced to sell at low prices. They also did not have proper storage facilities to keep back their produce for selling later at a better price.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: What was the first of the four government measures to improve agricultural marketing (NCERT 5.4)?
cards.back: The first step was regulation of markets to create orderly and transparent marketing conditions.
cards.quote: The first step was regulation of markets to create orderly and transparent marketing conditions.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Second component is provision of ____ like roads, railways, warehouses, godowns, cold storages and processing units.
cards.back: Second component is provision of physical infrastructure facilities like roads, railways, warehouses, godowns, cold storages and processing units.
cards.quote: Second component is provision of physical infrastructure facilities like roads, railways, warehouses, godowns, cold storages and processing units.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: What did the Union Government launch in 2016 to connect mandis and RMYs?
cards.back: In 2016, Union Government launched a portal named e-National Agriculture Market (e-NAM), and a Pan-India online portal by connecting mandis and RMYs.
cards.quote: In 2016, Union Government launched a portal named e-National Agriculture Market (e-NAM), and a Pan-India online portal by connecting mandis and RMYs.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Whose milk cooperatives show the role of cooperatives in transforming the rural landscape (NCERT 5.4)?
cards.back: The success of milk cooperatives in transforming the social and economic landscape of Gujarat and some other parts of the country is testimony to the role of cooperatives.
cards.quote: The success of milk cooperatives in transforming the social and economic landscape of Gujarat and some other parts of the country is testimony to the role of cooperatives.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Why have cooperatives received a setback in agricultural marketing in the recent past?
cards.back:
inadequate coverage of farmer members
lack of appropriate link between marketing and processing cooperatives
inefficient financial management
cards.quote: However cooperatives have received a setback during the recent past due to inadequate coverage of farmer members, lack of appropriate link between marketing and processing cooperatives and inefficient financial management.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Name the policy instruments, the fourth element of government measures in agricultural marketing.
cards.back:
assurance of minimum support prices (MSP) for agricultural products
maintenance of buffer stocks of wheat and rice by Food Corporation of India
distribution of food grains and sugar through PDS
cards.quote: The fourth element is the policy instruments like (i) assurance of minimum support prices (MSP) for agricultural products (ii) maintenance of buffer stocks of wheat and rice by Food Corporation of India and (iii) distribution of food grains and sugar through PDS.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Name examples of emerging alternate marketing channels where farmers sell directly to consumers.
cards.back:
Apni Mandi (Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan)
Hadaspar Mandi (Pune)
Rythu Bazars (vegetable and fruit markets in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana)
Uzhavar Sandies (farmers markets in Tamil Nadu)
cards.quote: Some examples of these channels are Apni Mandi (Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan); Hadaspar Mandi (Pune); Rythu Bazars (vegetable and fruit markets in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana) and Uzhavar Sandies (farmers markets in Tamil Nadu).

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: What do fast food chains provide farmers who join their contracts or alliances?
cards.back: providing them with not only seeds and other inputs but also assured procurement of the produce at predecided prices.
cards.quote: providing them with not only seeds and other inputs but also assured procurement of the produce at predecided prices.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Types: the two aspects that diversification includes.
cards.back:
change in cropping pattern
a shift of workforce from agriculture to other allied activities (livestock, poultry, fisheries etc.) and non-agriculture sector
cards.quote: Diversification includes two aspects one relates to change in cropping pattern and the other relates to a shift of workforce from agriculture to other allied activities (livestock, poultry, fisheries etc.) and non-agriculture sector.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: The need for diversification arises from the fact that there is ____ in depending exclusively on farming for livelihood.
cards.back: The need for diversification arises from the fact that there is greater risk in depending exclusively on farming for livelihood.
cards.quote: The need for diversification arises from the fact that there is greater risk in depending exclusively on farming for livelihood.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Name the dynamic sub-sectors of the non-farm economy.
cards.back:
agro-processing industries
food processing industries
leather industry
tourism
cards.quote: The dynamic sub-sectors include agro-processing industries, food processing industries, leather industry, tourism, etc.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Which farming system does India's farming community use, per NCERT's animal husbandry section (5.5)?
cards.back: In India, the farming community uses the mixed crop-livestock farming system
cards.quote: In India, the farming community uses the mixed crop-livestock farming system

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Name what livestock production provides to the family.
cards.back:
increased stability in income
food security
transport
fuel
nutrition for the family
cards.quote: Livestock production provides increased stability in income, food security, transport, fuel and nutrition for the family without disrupting other food-producing activities.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: By how much did milk production increase between 1951-2021, and what was the main reason?
cards.back: Milk production in the country has increased by about twelve times between 1951-2021. This can be attributed mainly to the successful implementation of Operation Flood.
cards.quote: Milk production in the country has increased by about twelve times between 1951-2021. This can be attributed mainly to the successful implementation of Operation Flood.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: What is Operation Flood?
cards.back: It is a system whereby all the farmers can pool their milk produced according to different grading (based on quality), processed and marketed to urban centres through cooperatives.
cards.quote: It is a system whereby all the farmers can pool their milk produced according to different grading (based on quality), processed and marketed to urban centres through cooperatives.
cards.note: Operation Flood is the system NCERT credits for the twelvefold rise in milk production between 1951 and 2021.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Name the major milk producing states of India.
cards.back:
Gujarat
Madhya Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh
Andhra Pradesh
Maharashtra
Punjab
Rajasthan
cards.quote: Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Punjab and Rajasthan, are major milk producing states.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Fish production from inland sources contributes about ____ to the total value of fish production
cards.back: Fish production from inland sources contributes about 75 per cent to the total value of fish production
cards.quote: Fish production from inland sources contributes about 75 per cent to the total value of fish production

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Name the major fish producing states of India.
cards.back:
West Bengal
Andhra Pradesh
Kerala
Gujarat
Maharashtra
Tamil Nadu
cards.quote: In India, West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu are major fish producing states.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Name the major problems the fishing community faces today.
cards.back:
Rampant underemployment
low per capita earnings
absence of mobility of labour to other sectors
a high rate of illiteracy and indebtedness
cards.quote: Rampant underemployment, low per capita earnings, absence of mobility of labour to other sectors and a high rate of illiteracy and indebtedness are some of the major problems fishing community face today.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Types: the diverse horticultural crops India grows.
cards.back:
fruits
vegetables
tuber crops
flowers
medicinal and aromatic plants
spices
plantation crops
cards.quote: Blessed with a varying climate and soil conditions, India has adopted growing of diverse horticultural crops such as fruits, vegetables, tuber crops, flowers, medicinal and aromatic plants, spices and plantation crops.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Enhancing the role of horticulture needs investment in which infrastructure?
cards.back:
electricity
cold storage systems
marketing linkages
small-scale processing units
technology improvement and dissemination
cards.quote: Enhancing its role requires investment in infrastructure like electricity, cold storage systems, marketing linkages, small-scale processing units and technology improvement and dissemination.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: How does IT positively impact the agriculture sector?
cards.back: It also has a positive impact on the agriculture sector as it can disseminate information regarding emerging technologies and its applications, prices, weather and soil conditions for growing different crops etc.
cards.quote: It also has a positive impact on the agriculture sector as it can disseminate information regarding emerging technologies and its applications, prices, weather and soil conditions for growing different crops etc.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: What harm do chemical fertilisers and toxic pesticides of conventional agriculture cause?
cards.back:
enter the food supply
penetrate the water sources
harm the livestock
deplete the soil
devastate natural eco-systems
cards.quote: Conventional agriculture relies heavily on chemical fertilisers and toxic pesticides etc., which enter the food supply, penetrate the water sources, harm the livestock, deplete the soil and devastate natural eco-systems.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Which eco-friendly technology does NCERT name as essential for sustainable development (Section 5.6)?
cards.back: Efforts in evolving technologies which are eco-friendly are essential for sustainable development and one such technology which is eco-friendly is organic farming.
cards.quote: Efforts in evolving technologies which are eco-friendly are essential for sustainable development and one such technology which is eco-friendly is organic farming.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Define organic agriculture: NCERT calls it 'a whole system of' what?
cards.back: farming that restores, maintains and enhances the ecological balance.
cards.quote: farming that restores, maintains and enhances the ecological balance.
cards.note: NCERT: organic agriculture is a whole system of farming that restores, maintains and enhances the ecological balance.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Name the benefits of organic farming.
cards.back:
substitute costlier agricultural inputs (such as HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, pesticides etc.) with locally produced organic inputs that are cheaper
generates income through exports
organically grown food has more nutritional value than chemical farming
requires more labour input than conventional farming
the produce is pesticide-free and produced in an environmentally sustainable way
cards.quote: Organic agriculture offers a means to substitute costlier agricultural inputs (such as HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, pesticides etc.) with locally produced organic inputs that are cheaper and thereby generate good returns on investment. Organic agriculture also generates income through exports as the demand for organically grown crops is on a rise. Studies across countries have shown that organically grown food has more nutritional value than chemical farming thus providing us with healthy foods. Since organic farming requires more labour input than conventional farming, India will find organic farming an attractive proposition. Finally, the produce is pesticide-free and produced in an environmentally sustainable way

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Name the limitations or problems farmers face with organic farming, especially in the initial years.
cards.back:
the yields from organic farming are less than modern agricultural farming in the initial years
small and marginal farmers may find it difficult to adapt to largescale production
Organic produce may also have more blemishes and a shorter shelf life than sprayed produce
choice in production of off-season crops is quite limited in organic farming
cards.quote: It has been observed that the yields from organic farming are less than modern agricultural farming in the initial years. Therefore, small and marginal farmers may find it difficult to adapt to largescale production. Organic produce may also have more blemishes and a shorter shelf life than sprayed produce. Moreover choice in production of off-season crops is quite limited in organic farming.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Rural areas can be made more vibrant through diversification into which activities?
cards.back:
dairying
poultry
fisheries
vegetables and fruits
cards.quote: through diversification into dairying, poultry, fisheries, vegetables and fruits

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Name the elements essential to realise the full potential of the rural sector.
cards.back:
infrastructure elements like credit and marketing
farmer-friendly agricultural policies
a constant appraisal and dialogue between farmers' groups and state agricultural departments
cards.quote: infrastructure elements like credit and marketing, farmer-friendly agricultural policies and a constant appraisal and dialogue between farmers' groups and state agricultural departments are essential to realise the full potential of the sector.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Name the 4 defining features of a perfectly competitive market.
cards.back:
1. The market consists of a large number of buyers and sellers
2. Each firm produces and sells a homogenous product
3. Entry into the market as well as exit from the market are free for firms
4. Information is perfect
cards.quote: A perfectly competitive market has the following defining features: 1. The market consists of a large number of buyers and sellers 2. Each firm produces and sells a homogenous product. i.e., the product of one firm cannot be differentiated from the product of any other firm. 3. Entry into the market as well as exit from the market are free for firms. 4. Information is perfect.
cards.note: Many buyers and sellers, identical product, free entry and exit, perfect information.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: ____ mean that it is easy for firms to enter the market, as well as to leave it.
cards.back: Free entry and exit mean that it is easy for firms to enter the market, as well as to leave it.
cards.quote: Free entry and exit mean that it is easy for firms to enter the market, as well as to leave it.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: What does perfect information imply in a perfectly competitive market?
cards.back: Perfect information implies that all buyers and all sellers are completely informed about the price, quality and other relevant details about the product, as well as the market.
cards.quote: Perfect information implies that all buyers and all sellers are completely informed about the price, quality and other relevant details about the product, as well as the market.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: What is the single most distinguishing characteristic of perfect competition?
cards.back: the single most distinguishing characteristic of perfect competition: price taking behaviour.
cards.quote: These features result in the single most distinguishing characteristic of perfect competition: price taking behaviour.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: What does a price-taking firm believe happens if it sets a price above the market price?
cards.back: A price-taking firm believes that if it sets a price above the market price, it will be unable to sell any quantity of the good that it produces.
cards.quote: A price-taking firm believes that if it sets a price above the market price, it will be unable to sell any quantity of the good that it produces.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: What is the 'price line'?
cards.back: Since the market price is fixed at p, we obtain a horizontal straight line that cuts the y-axis at a height equal to p. This horizontal straight line is called the price line.
cards.quote: Since the market price is fixed at p, we obtain a horizontal straight line that cuts the y-axis at a height equal to p. This horizontal straight line is called the price line.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: How is a firm's profit defined?
cards.back: the difference between its total revenue (TR) and its total cost of production (TC).
cards.quote: is defined to be the difference between its total revenue (TR) and its total cost of production (TC).

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Consumers' income rises (market for clothes, a normal good): what happens to the demand curve?
cards.back: Here we consider the example of a normal good like clothes, the demand for which increases with increase in income of consumers, thereby causing a rightward shift in the demand curve.
cards.quote: Here we consider the example of a normal good like clothes, the demand for which increases with increase in income of consumers, thereby causing a rightward shift in the demand curve.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Consumers' income rises (clothes): effect on equilibrium price and quantity?
cards.back: at the new equilibrium, the price of clothes is higher and the quantity demanded and sold is also higher
cards.quote: at the new equilibrium, the price of clothes is higher and the quantity demanded and sold is also higher

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Formula: profit (π) of a firm.
cards.back:
π = TR – TC
the difference between its total revenue (TR) and its total cost of production (TC).
cards.quote: is defined to be the difference between its total revenue (TR) and its total cost of production (TC). In other words π = TR – TC

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: The number of consumers in the market for clothes increases: effect on the demand curve?
cards.back: As the number of consumers increases, other factors remaining unchanged, at each price, more clothes will be demanded. Thus, the demand curve will shift rightwards.
cards.quote: As the number of consumers increases, other factors remaining unchanged, at each price, more clothes will be demanded. Thus, the demand curve will shift rightwards.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: When the supply curve shifts, do equilibrium price and quantity change in the same or opposite directions?
cards.back: Notice the directions of change in price and quantity are opposite whenever there is a shift in supply curve.
cards.quote: Notice the directions of change in price and quantity are opposite whenever there is a shift in supply curve.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: The price of an input used in production rises: effect on the supply curve?
cards.back: This will increase the marginal cost of production of the firms using this input. Therefore, at each price, the market supply will be less than before. Hence, the supply curve shifts leftward.
cards.quote: This will increase the marginal cost of production of the firms using this input. Therefore, at each price, the market supply will be less than before. Hence, the supply curve shifts leftward.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Input price rises (supply shifts left, demand unchanged): effect on equilibrium price and quantity?
cards.back: As a result, compared to the old equilibrium, now the market price rises and quantity produced decreases.
cards.quote: As a result, compared to the old equilibrium, now the market price rises and quantity produced decreases.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: In the short run, what must price exceed for a firm to continue to produce?
cards.back: For the firm to continue to produce, in the short run, price must be greater than the average variable cost (p > AVC)
cards.quote: For the firm to continue to produce, in the short run, price must be greater than the average variable cost (p > AVC)

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: The number of firms increases: effect on the supply curve and the demand curve?
cards.back: Since at each price now more firms will supply the commodity, the supply curve shifts to the right but it does not have any effect on the demand curve.
cards.quote: Since at each price now more firms will supply the commodity, the supply curve shifts to the right but it does not have any effect on the demand curve.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Define a firm's 'supply'.
cards.back: A firm's 'supply' is the quantity that it chooses to sell at a given price, given technology, and given the prices of factors of production.
cards.quote: A firm's 'supply' is the quantity that it chooses to sell at a given price, given technology, and given the prices of factors of production.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: The number of firms increases: effect on equilibrium price and quantity?
cards.back: there will be a decrease in price of the commodity and increase in the quantity produced compared to the initial situation
cards.quote: there will be a decrease in price of the commodity and increase in the quantity produced compared to the initial situation

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Name the 2 cases in which supply and demand curves shift simultaneously in opposite directions.
cards.back:
(iii) Supply curve shifts leftward and demand curve shifts rightward.
(iv) Supply curve shifts rightward and demand curve shifts leftward.
cards.quote: (iii) Supply curve shifts leftward and demand curve shifts rightward. (iv) Supply curve shifts rightward and demand curve shifts leftward.

source.section: Simultaneous Shifts of Demand and Supply

cards.note: Same-direction shifts fix the effect on quantity; opposite-direction shifts fix the effect on price (Table 5.1).

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: A table describing the quantities sold by a firm at various prices, technology and prices of factors remaining unchanged, is called a ____.
cards.back: supply schedule. A table describing the quantities sold by a firm at various prices, technology and prices of factors remaining unchanged, is called a supply schedule.
cards.quote: A table describing the quantities sold by a firm at various prices, technology and prices of factors remaining unchanged, is called a supply schedule.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: What does the supply curve of a firm show?
cards.back: The supply curve of a firm shows the levels of output (plotted on the x-axis) that the firm chooses to produce corresponding to different values of the market price (plotted on the y-axis), again keeping technology and prices of factors of production unchanged.
cards.quote: The supply curve of a firm shows the levels of output (plotted on the x-axis) that the firm chooses to produce corresponding to different values of the market price (plotted on the y-axis), again keeping technology and prices of factors of production unchanged.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Both demand and supply curves shift rightward: effect on equilibrium quantity and price?
cards.back: due to a rightward shift in both demand and supply curves, the equilibrium quantity increases invariably but the equilibrium price may either increase, decrease or remain unchanged
cards.quote: due to a rightward shift in both demand and supply curves, the equilibrium quantity increases invariably but the equilibrium price may either increase, decrease or remain unchanged

source.section: Simultaneous Shifts of Demand and Supply

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Simultaneous shifts: same direction vs opposite directions. Which of price and quantity is unambiguous?
cards.back: In the first two cases which are shown in the first two rows of the table, the impact on equilibrium quantity is unambiguous but the equilibrium price may change, if at all, in either direction depending on the magnitudes of shifts. In the next two cases, shown in the last two rows of the table, the effect on price is unambiguous whereas effect on quantity depends on the magnitude of shifts in the two curves.
cards.quote: In the first two cases which are shown in the first two rows of the table, the impact on equilibrium quantity is unambiguous but the equilibrium price may change, if at all, in either direction depending on the magnitudes of shifts. In the next two cases, shown in the last two rows of the table, the effect on price is unambiguous whereas effect on quantity depends on the magnitude of shifts in the two curves.

source.section: Simultaneous Shifts of Demand and Supply

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Types of supply curve of a firm.
cards.back:
short run supply curve
long run supply curve
cards.quote: We distinguish between the short run supply curve and the long run supply curve.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: What is the short run shut down point of a firm?
cards.back: the last price-output combination at which the firm produces positive output is the point of minimum AVC where the SMC curve cuts the AVC curve. Below this, there will be no production. This point is called the short run shut down point of the firm.
cards.quote: the last price-output combination at which the firm produces positive output is the point of minimum AVC where the SMC curve cuts the AVC curve. Below this, there will be no production. This point is called the short run shut down point of the firm.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Define normal profit.
cards.back: The minimum level of profit that is needed to keep a firm in the existing business is defined as normal profit.
cards.quote: The minimum level of profit that is needed to keep a firm in the existing business is defined as normal profit.

source.section: 4.4.4 The Normal Profit and Break-even Point

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Profit that a firm earns over and above the normal profit is called the ____.
cards.back: super-normal profit. Profit that a firm earns over and above the normal profit is called the super-normal profit.
cards.quote: Profit that a firm earns over and above the normal profit is called the super-normal profit.

source.section: 4.4.4 The Normal Profit and Break-even Point

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: In the ____, a firm does not produce if it earns anything less than the normal profit.
cards.back: In the long run, a firm does not produce if it earns anything less than the normal profit.
cards.quote: In the long run, a firm does not produce if it earns anything less than the normal profit.

source.section: 4.4.4 The Normal Profit and Break-even Point

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: What is the break-even point of a firm?
cards.back: The point on the supply curve at which a firm earns only normal profit is called the break-even point of the firm.
cards.quote: The point on the supply curve at which a firm earns only normal profit is called the break-even point of the firm.

source.section: 4.4.4 The Normal Profit and Break-even Point

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Steps: how supernormal profit is wiped out under free entry, in order.
cards.back:
The possibility of earning supernormal profit will attract some new firms.
As new firms enter the market supply curve shifts rightward.
However, demand remains unchanged.
This causes market price to fall.
As prices fall, supernormal profits are eventually wiped out.
cards.quote: The possibility of earning supernormal profit will attract some new firms. As new firms enter the market supply curve shifts rightward. However, demand remains unchanged. This causes market price to fall. As prices fall, supernormal profits are eventually wiped out.

source.section: Market Equilibrium: Free Entry and Exit

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Which point on the supply curve is the break-even point of a firm (LRAC, or SAC in the short run)?
cards.back: The point of minimum average cost at which the supply curve cuts the LRAC curve (in short run, SAC curve) is therefore the break-even point of a firm.
cards.quote: The point of minimum average cost at which the supply curve cuts the LRAC curve (in short run, SAC curve) is therefore the break-even point of a firm.

source.section: 4.4.4 The Normal Profit and Break-even Point

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Perfect competition with free entry and exit: what profit will each firm always earn, in NCERT's term?
cards.back: With free entry and exit, each firm will always earn normal profit
cards.quote: With free entry and exit, each firm will always earn normal profit

source.section: Market Equilibrium: Free Entry and Exit

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Any factor that affects a firm's ____ is of course a determinant of its supply curve.
cards.back: Any factor that affects a firm's marginal cost curve is of course a determinant of its supply curve.
cards.quote: Any factor that affects a firm's marginal cost curve is of course a determinant of its supply curve.

source.section: 4.5 Determinants of a Firm's Supply Curve

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Under free entry and exit, what happens to firms at prices above and below the minimum average cost?
cards.back: Therefore, at prices greater than the minimum average cost, new firms will enter, and at prices below minimum average cost, existing firms will start exiting.
cards.quote: Therefore, at prices greater than the minimum average cost, new firms will enter, and at prices below minimum average cost, existing firms will start exiting.

source.section: Market Equilibrium: Free Entry and Exit

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: How does technological progress shift a firm's supply curve?
cards.back: As the firm's supply curve is essentially a segment of the MC curve, technological progress shifts the supply curve of the firm to the right. At any given market price, the firm now supplies more units of output.
cards.quote: As the firm's supply curve is essentially a segment of the MC curve, technological progress shifts the supply curve of the firm to the right. At any given market price, the firm now supplies more units of output.

source.section: 4.5 Determinants of a Firm's Supply Curve

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: How does a rise in the price of an input shift a firm's supply curve?
cards.back: that is, there is a leftward (or upward) shift of the MC curve. This means that the firm's supply curve shifts to the left: at any given market price, the firm now supplies fewer units of output.
cards.quote: that is, there is a leftward (or upward) shift of the MC curve. This means that the firm's supply curve shifts to the left: at any given market price, the firm now supplies fewer units of output.

source.section: 4.5 Determinants of a Firm's Supply Curve

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: At the price level equal to the minimum average cost of the firms, each firm will earn ____
cards.back: At the price level equal to the minimum average cost of the firms, each firm will earn normal profit
cards.quote: At the price level equal to the minimum average cost of the firms, each firm will earn normal profit

source.section: Market Equilibrium: Free Entry and Exit

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: What is a unit tax?
cards.back: A unit tax is a tax that the government imposes per unit sale of output.
cards.quote: A unit tax is a tax that the government imposes per unit sale of output.

source.section: 4.5 Determinants of a Firm's Supply Curve

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Formula: market price under free entry and exit of firms.
cards.back: p = min AC
cards.quote: always be equal to the minimum average cost, that is p = min AC

source.section: Market Equilibrium: Free Entry and Exit

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Free entry and exit: the equilibrium price equals min AC. What determines the equilibrium quantity supplied?
cards.back: In equilibrium, the quantity supplied will be determined by the market demand at that price so that they are equal.
cards.quote: In equilibrium, the quantity supplied will be determined by the market demand at that price so that they are equal.

source.section: Market Equilibrium: Free Entry and Exit

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: A unit tax of Rs t is imposed. What happens to a firm's long run AC and MC at any output?
cards.back: Since the firm must pay an extra Rs t for each unit of the good produced, the firm's long run average cost and long run marginal cost at any level of output increases by Rs t.
cards.quote: Since the firm must pay an extra Rs t for each unit of the good produced, the firm's long run average cost and long run marginal cost at any level of output increases by Rs t.

source.section: 4.5 Determinants of a Firm's Supply Curve

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Under free entry and exit, how is the equilibrium number of firms in the market determined?
cards.back: Therefore, the equilibrium number of firms in the market is equal to the number of firms required to supply q0 output at p0, each in turn supplying q0f amount at that price.
cards.quote: Therefore, the equilibrium number of firms in the market is equal to the number of firms required to supply q0 output at p0, each in turn supplying q0f amount at that price.

source.section: Market Equilibrium: Free Entry and Exit

cards.note: n0 = q0 / q0f: equilibrium output divided by what each firm supplies at that price.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: How does a unit tax shift a firm's long run supply curve?
cards.back: Notice that the unit tax shifts the firm's long run supply curve to the left: at any given market price, the firm now supplies fewer units of output.
cards.quote: Notice that the unit tax shifts the firm's long run supply curve to the left: at any given market price, the firm now supplies fewer units of output.

source.section: 4.5 Determinants of a Firm's Supply Curve

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: How is market supply at price p related to the supplies of individual firms?
cards.back: In other words, the market supply at price p is the summation of the supplies of individual firms at that price.
cards.quote: In other words, the market supply at price p is the summation of the supplies of individual firms at that price.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Formula: output produced by n firms in aggregate at market price p.
cards.back: [supply of firm 1 at price p] + [supply of firm 2 at price p] + ... + [supply of firm n at price p]
cards.quote: Then, the output produced by the n firms in aggregate is [supply of firm 1 at price p] + [supply of firm 2 at price p] + ... + [supply of firm n at price p].

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Formula: market supply Sm(p) in a market with two firms.
cards.back: Sm(p) = S1(p) + S2(p)
cards.quote: Now, the market supply curve, Sm(p), simply sums up the supply curves of the two firms; in other words Sm(p) = S1(p) + S2(p)

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Free entry and exit: demand shifts rightwards (leftwards). Effect on quantity, number of firms and price?
cards.back: Thus, due to a shift in demand rightwards (leftwards), the equilibrium quantity and number of firms will increase (decrease) whereas the equilibrium price will remain unchanged.
cards.quote: Thus, due to a shift in demand rightwards (leftwards), the equilibrium quantity and number of firms will increase (decrease) whereas the equilibrium price will remain unchanged.

source.section: Shifts in Demand (Free Entry and Exit)

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: How does a change in the number of firms shift the market supply curve?
cards.back: Specifically, if the number of firms in the market increases (decreases), the market supply curve shifts to the right (left).
cards.quote: Specifically, if the number of firms in the market increases (decreases), the market supply curve shifts to the right (left).

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Define the price elasticity of supply of a good.
cards.back: The price elasticity of supply of a good measures the responsiveness of quantity supplied to changes in the price of the good.
cards.quote: The price elasticity of supply of a good measures the responsiveness of quantity supplied to changes in the price of the good.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Demand shift: fixed number of firms vs free entry and exit. Difference in the effect on quantity and price?
cards.back: with free entry and exit, shift in demand has a larger effect on quantity than it does with the fixed number of firms. But unlike with fixed number of firms, here, we do not have any effect on equilibrium price at all.
cards.quote: with free entry and exit, shift in demand has a larger effect on quantity than it does with the fixed number of firms. But unlike with fixed number of firms, here, we do not have any effect on equilibrium price at all.

source.section: Shifts in Demand (Free Entry and Exit)

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Formula: price elasticity of supply (eS).
cards.back: Price elasticity of supply, eS = Percentage change in quantity supplied / Percentage change in price
cards.quote: Price elasticity of supply, eS = Percentage change in quantity supplied Percentage change in price

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: When the supply curve is ____, supply is completely insensitive to price and the elasticity of supply is ____.
cards.back: When the supply curve is vertical, supply is completely insensitive to price and the elasticity of supply is zero.
cards.quote: When the supply curve is vertical, supply is completely insensitive to price and the elasticity of supply is zero.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Does the price elasticity of supply depend on the units of measurement?
cards.back: Like the price elasticity of demand, the price elasticity of supply is also independent of units.
cards.quote: Like the price elasticity of demand, the price elasticity of supply is also independent of units.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: A straight-line supply curve cuts the quantity-axis at its negative range (Fig. 4.14a). Its eS at any point?
cards.back: The elasticity at any point on such a supply curve, therefore, will be greater than 1.
cards.quote: The elasticity at any point on such a supply curve, therefore, will be greater than 1.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: A straight-line supply curve cuts the quantity-axis at its positive range (Fig. 4.14c). Its eS at any point?
cards.back: Now, Mq0 < Oq0 and hence, eS < 1. S can be any point on the supply curve, and therefore at all points on such a supply curve eS < 1.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: A straight-line supply curve passes through the origin (Fig. 4.14b). Its eS at any point?
cards.back: At any point on a straight line, supply curve going through the origin price elasticity will be one.
cards.quote: At any point on a straight line, supply curve going through the origin price elasticity will be one.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: The demand curve that a firm faces in a perfectly competitive market is ____; it is a horizontal straight line at the market price.
cards.back: The demand curve that a firm faces in a perfectly competitive market is perfectly elastic; it is a horizontal straight line at the market price.
cards.quote: The demand curve that a firm faces in a perfectly competitive market is perfectly elastic; it is a horizontal straight line at the market price.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Name the 3 conditions for short run profit maximisation at a positive output level.
cards.back:
(i) p = SMC
(ii) SMC is non-decreasing
(iii) p ≥ AVC
cards.quote: If there is a positive level of output at which a firm's profit is maximised in the short run, three conditions must hold at that output level (i) p = SMC (ii) SMC is non-decreasing (iii) p ≥ AVC.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Fixed number of firms, supply unchanged: demand shifts rightward (leftward). Effect on quantity and price?
cards.back: With supply curve remaining unchanged when demand curve shifts rightward (leftward), the equilibrium quantity increases (decreases) and equilibrium price increases (decreases) with fixed number of firms.
cards.quote: With supply curve remaining unchanged when demand curve shifts rightward (leftward), the equilibrium quantity increases (decreases) and equilibrium price increases (decreases) with fixed number of firms.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Name the 3 conditions for long run profit maximisation at a positive output level.
cards.back:
(i) p = LRMC
(ii) LRMC is non-decreasing
(iii) p ≥ LRAC
cards.quote: If there is a positive level of output at which a firm's profit is maximised in the long run, three conditions must hold at that output level (i) p = LRMC (ii) LRMC is non-decreasing (iii) p ≥ LRAC.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: What is the short run supply curve of a firm?
cards.back: The short run supply curve of a firm is the rising part of the SMC curve from and above minimum AVC together with 0 output for all prices less than the minimum AVC.
cards.quote: The short run supply curve of a firm is the rising part of the SMC curve from and above minimum AVC together with 0 output for all prices less than the minimum AVC.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Fixed number of firms, demand unchanged: supply shifts rightward (leftward). Effect on quantity and price?
cards.back: With demand curve remaining unchanged when supply curve shifts rightward (leftward), the equilibrium quantity increases (decreases) and equilibrium price decreases (increases) with fixed number of firms.
cards.quote: With demand curve remaining unchanged when supply curve shifts rightward (leftward), the equilibrium quantity increases (decreases) and equilibrium price decreases (increases) with fixed number of firms.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: What is the long run supply curve of a firm?
cards.back: The long run supply curve of a firm is the rising part of the LRMC curve from and above minimum LRAC together with 0 output for all prices less than the minimum LRAC.
cards.quote: The long run supply curve of a firm is the rising part of the LRMC curve from and above minimum LRAC together with 0 output for all prices less than the minimum LRAC.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: When both demand and supply curves shift in the same direction, the effect on equilibrium ____ can be unambiguously determined
cards.back: When both demand and supply curves shift in the same direction, the effect on equilibrium quantity can be unambiguously determined
cards.quote: When both demand and supply curves shift in the same direction, the effect on equilibrium quantity can be unambiguously determined

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: How is the market supply curve obtained?
cards.back: The market supply curve is obtained by the horizontal summation of the supply curves of individual firms.
cards.quote: The market supply curve is obtained by the horizontal summation of the supply curves of individual firms.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
cards.front: When demand and supply curves shift in opposite directions, the effect on equilibrium ____ can be unambiguously determined
cards.back: When demand and supply curves shift in opposite directions, the effect on equilibrium price can be unambiguously determined
cards.quote: When demand and supply curves shift in opposite directions, the effect on equilibrium price can be unambiguously determined
